title: Implement a Small Issue
bottom_line: For a small, obvious GitHub issue labeled `ai`: it implements the fix and opens a PR, skipping the full review and test-plan cycle.

sections.heading: Use the lite path only for small, obvious fixes

cards.title: Use impl-issue-lite
cards.text: A few-line fix, a single well-scoped change, no design decision to make. A separate review pass and formal test plan would be overkill.

cards.title: Use impl-issue instead
cards.text: The issue spans several files or components, involves a design or ordering decision, or the approach is not obvious.

blocks.caption: If the issue turns out not to be small once read in full, the command stops and tells you to use `/plan-tools:impl-issue`.

blocks.text: It is the same as `/plan-tools:impl-issue` for one small, mechanically obvious residual work item (an `ai` issue), except that it skips the full `finalize-pr` cycle: its code review, its formal test plan and its recording of leftover work as new issues.

sections.heading: Run it bare for your oldest issue, or name one

blocks.caption: Every part is optional. The issue number and the model can come in either order.

blocks.title: What you can pass
rows: Your oldest open issue with the label
The model the helper runs on. One of `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`.
Looks for issues with `<name>` instead of `ai`.

blocks.title: Which issue it works on

nodes.label: Oldest open labeled issue you opened

blocks.caption: Without a number, it only looks at open issues with the label that you opened. If there are none, it never picks a different issue.

blocks.title: Defaults shared across the plugin
rows: Deferred work goes into GitHub issues labeled `ai`
A model word in the arguments, for example `opus`

cards.title: git and GitHub CLI
cards.text: Install `git` and `gh`, signed in with `gh auth login`, with push access to the repository. Every issue, PR and status command goes through `gh`.

cards.title: A small issue
cards.text: An open GitHub issue labeled `ai` (or your `--label` name) that is small and mechanically obvious.

sections.heading: A helper checks the size, builds the fix and opens the PR

steps.title: Reads the whole issue
steps.text: One helper, on the chosen model, fetches the issue and reads it in full before writing any code.

steps.title: Confirms it is trivial
steps.text: If the change is not small and mechanically obvious, it stops and reports that the issue needs `/plan-tools:impl-issue` instead.

steps.title: Starts a fresh branch
steps.text: It branches from the latest version of the repository's default branch. It detects that branch's name and never assumes `main`.

steps.title: Builds exactly what the issue asks
steps.text: No extra features, refactors or files beyond what the issue describes.

steps.title: Checks the work, then commits
steps.text: Existing tests and build must pass, as applicable to the repository. It commits only complete work, never partial work, with a `Closes #<number>` line in the commit message.

steps.title: Pushes and opens the PR
steps.text: The PR has a title and body summarizing the change and carries the `Closes #<number>` line. If you have not already said yes to pushing in this session, it confirms the branch and base and asks first.

sections.heading: It stops without pushing if the issue is big or checks fail

cards.title: No issue found
cards.text: It stops and tells you. It does not fall back to a different issue.

cards.title: Issue is not trivial
cards.text: It stops without pushing or opening a PR.

cards.title: A check fails
cards.text: If any verification step fails, such as tests or build, it stops and reports back without pushing or opening a PR.

sections.heading: You get a summary, the closed issue number and the PR link

before.label: Before
before.text: An open, small GitHub issue labeled `ai`.

after.label: After
after.text: A PR for that issue, carrying `Closes #<number>`, so merging it closes the issue.

blocks.text: The helper's summary is passed to you as it is, with no extra commentary or next steps it did not report.
